messages.text: Hey, we have done a lot of code changes in the last 24 to 48 hours. Can you please go through each and every commit that we have done? I think there have been more than 10 to 15 commits in all, starting with all the S series, going all the way to onboarding flow, refactoring the intent routing, the different fixes, Play Store submissions. That's about the last 24 hours commits. Not exhaustive, but yeah, you know what I'm trying to do. Deeply, thoroughly, comprehensively analyze the entire code, evaluate it, analyze the code before it, analyze all the functionalities of HiD, look at all the bugs that we have logged in the debug log and try to see if any of them are still there or not. Okay, maybe you can skip that part, but yeah, just to get an idea of where we have gone wrong in the past. Ensure there are no app crashes, all the code is written correctly, all the features are written correctly, there have been no misses, there were a lot of context compactions in our process, so we want to ensure that we haven't missed any angle. Be very thorough in your entire evaluation, take it step by step, but I want you to cover all the possible grounds and do the high confidence fixes that you think that are must do and call out the ones that are to be observed and then fixed that looks suspicious to you. Again, as I said, use your highest level of reasoning and thinking and be very detailed in your response too. For each and every bug fixed, share a before and after, share a detailed report of each bug that has been fixed and log each bug in the debug log again.

I’ll treat this like a full recent-change audit rather than a quick pass: first I’ll map the last 48 hours of commits and touched areas, then inspect the debug log/history, run the available verification, and only make fixes where the evidence is strong. After that I’ll update the debug log with each confirmed fix plus call out anything that remains observational.

The initial map shows 21 commits in the last 48 hours, from `R2+R3` through `S12`, and the only current working-tree noise is an untracked `handy_macos_ref/` reference folder. I’m going to anchor the review on the parent of the oldest recent commit so I can compare “before” versus “after” without disturbing anything.

The aggregate diff is large: 169 files, about 12.8k insertions, across recipes, intent/action policy, onboarding, production hardening, evals, and Play Store docs. I’m starting verification now in parallel with reading the relevant code, because compile/test failures will tell us where to dig first.

Plain Gradle can’t start because macOS has no Java runtime on `PATH`, which matches the project’s own recent debug-log notes. I’m switching to the repo-local JDK path used by the last successful validations, then I’ll run the full local suite plus lint/assembly.

The local JDK verification is green for unit tests, lint, and debug assembly, though it reused most cached outputs. I’m moving from “does it compile” to “could this still be wrong in production” now: routing ambiguity, unsafe native actions, date/time parsing, onboarding entry points, and recipe execution are the highest-risk seams from these commits.

I found one strong, user-facing miss: the new canonical recipes can be emitted by the assistant, but the execution gate still only recognizes older verbs like tap/open/type/search/scroll. That means requests such as “set a 10-minute timer”, “install Spotify”, “schedule dentist tomorrow”, “book a cab”, “turn on DND”, and “find cheap saree on Meesho” could produce a recipe directive and then be silently ignored as “guidance-only.”

I’m going to fix that gate now and pin it with tests. The shape is small but important: expand the “explicit action” verb set to match the canonical recipes, while keeping the existing help-only blocks so “how do I…” and “where is…” still stay guidance-only.

The focused gate test passes after the change. I’m continuing the audit now, especially around the recent “help me read this”/summarize mode, LLM tool routing, and onboarding because those are the places context compaction tends to leave subtle wiring gaps.

A second must-fix popped out of the Play Store/compliance path: the submission doc and `HandySettings` both say reduced mode disables `dispatch_action`/intent firing, but both full chat and overlay always advertised `dispatch_action`. I’m going to wire that to the live Accessibility-service state and suppress recipe prompting/execution in reduced mode too, so the code matches the Play disclosure.

The app compile caught no wiring break after the reduced-mode change; the only compiler warnings are pre-existing deprecated `announceForAccessibility` calls in the floating widget service. I’m leaving those as observational because they aren’t crashy and changing accessibility announcements deserves a separate UI/device pass.

The full local suite is green after the fixes: `:core:test`, `:android-runtime:test`, `:app:test`, lint, and debug assembly all passed. I’m doing the Play/release-shaped validation and an emulator launch smoke next, then I’ll append the two new debug-log entries with before/after and validation details.

I reviewed the last 48 hours of history: 21 commits from `2ee317e R2+R3` through `2b78200 S12`. I made two must-fix changes and logged both in [DEBUG_LOG.md](/Users/satvik.bansal/Desktop/Handy.android/HandyV2/DEBUG_LOG.md:1379) as `DL-084` and [DEBUG_LOG.md](/Users/satvik.bansal/Desktop/Handy.android/HandyV2/DEBUG_LOG.md:1396) as `DL-085`.

**Fixed**
- `DL-084`: canonical S-series recipes could route correctly but still be ignored by the old “do-it-for-me” gate.
  Before: “set a 10-minute timer”, “install spotify”, “schedule dentist tomorrow”, “book a cab”, “find cheap saree”, etc. could emit `[INTENT:...]` and then silently do nothing.
  After: [UserGoal.kt](/Users/satvik.bansal/Desktop/Handy.android/HandyV2/core/src/main/kotlin/com/handy/core/agent/UserGoal.kt:80) now recognizes the canonical action verbs, while help-only wording still blocks execution.

- `DL-085`: reduced mode still advertised/allowed `dispatch_action` and quick-overlay recipes despite Play disclosure saying no Intents fire without Accessibility.
  Before: full chat and overlay always passed `intentDispatchEnabled = true`; quick overlay always appended recipe instructions.
  After: [ChatViewModel.kt](/Users/satvik.bansal/Desktop/Handy.android/HandyV2/app/src/main/kotlin/com/handy/app/chat/ChatViewModel.kt:351) and [OverlayChatPipeline.kt](/Users/satvik.bansal/Desktop/Handy.android/HandyV2/app/src/main/kotlin/com/handy/app/overlay/OverlayChatPipeline.kt:135) now gate automation on disclosure + live Accessibility state; [PromptCatalog.kt](/Users/satvik.bansal/Desktop/Handy.android/HandyV2/core/src/main/kotlin/com/handy/core/prompts/PromptCatalog.kt:342) can suppress recipe prompting, and overlay skips recipe routing defensively at [OverlayChatPipeline.kt](/Users/satvik.bansal/Desktop/Handy.android/HandyV2/app/src/main/kotlin/com/handy/app/overlay/OverlayChatPipeline.kt:243).

**Commit Audit**
- `R2+R3`, `R3+V2`: recipe/action/overlay foundations look structurally sound; policy checks and treeHash guards are in place.
- `E1`: eval/replay framework is valuable and passed at 100% on recorded suites.
- `OPS1`: retry/budget/redaction changes are covered; no current build break found.
- `PLAY1`: docs and Play disclosure mostly align now after the reduced-mode fix.
- `FIX-A` through `FIX-E`: fixes remain represented in tests/docs; no regression found.
- `O1`: onboarding’s reduced-mode path is coherent; no launch crash in emulator smoke.
- S-series recipe commits (`OpenApp`, `S2`, `S3`, `S4`, `S5`, `S6`, `S8`, `S9`, `S10`, `S12`): routing and unit coverage are strong; the missing execution-gate coverage was the key gap fixed in `DL-084`.

**Validation**
- `:core:test :android-runtime:test :app:test :app:lint :app:assembleDebug` passed.
- `:app:assembleRelease` passed, including R8/minified release.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Installed debug APK on `emulator-5554`; launching `OnboardingActivity` returned `Status: ok`, process stayed alive (`pid 18618`), and fresh `AndroidRuntime:E ActivityTaskManager:E Handy:E` logcat was empty.

**Watch Items**
- Only an emulator was available; real Pixel/Uber/Ola/Rapido/Gmail/WhatsApp manual recipe sweeps remain unverified.
- Two pre-existing deprecated `announceForAccessibility(...)` warnings remain in `FloatingWidgetOverlayService`; not crashy, but worth a later cleanup.
- `handy_macos_ref/` is still untracked; I left it untouched.
